newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-TOTTENHAM STALK JUNINHO AS ATLETICO BID CRUMBLES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TOTTENHAM STALK JUNINHO AS ATLETICO BID CRUMBLES.

text.p: Brazilian midfielder Juninho looked set to join English premier league Tottenham on Monday after his current club Middlesbrough confirmed they had accepted an 11 million pounds ($18.3 million) bid.
"We have accepted the bid from Tottenham and we have informed Juninho. It is now subject to him agreeing personal terms," said Dave Allen, Middlesbrough's public relations officer.

Tottenham's bid comes just days after they sold England striker Teddy Sheringham to premier league champions Manchester United, and is a record for the club. They are also negotiating with Newcastle for another England man, Les Ferdinand.
However, the London club would not comment on how far negotiations with the Brazilian had reached.
"All I can say is that the play is in play," said Tottenham's chief executive Claude Littner. "Who he goes to is up to him."
He denied reports that club officials would be going to Brazil to clinch the deal.
"With modern communications like the telephone it really isn't necessary for anyone to go. Besides, Juninho and his family aren't even in Brazil at the moment."

Juninho, who is leaving Middlesbrough after they were relegated from the premier league, is understood to favour a move to Spain where he feels greater exposure on television in Brazil will increase his chances of making the national squad for the 1998 World Cup finals.
But both Allen and Littner dismissed reports in Spanish newspapers on Monday that the Brazilian had signed for Atletico Madrid at the weekend.
"That is not true. At the moment Juninho is still a Middlesbrough player," said Allen. "Atletico made an offer some weeks ago but it was derisory.
"Tottenham are the only club we have accepted an offer from and the way is clear for them to discuss terms with Juninho."
